definition: An agentic loop is a repeating cycle: the AI looks at the situation, decides what to do next, takes an action with a tool, looks at the result, and repeats until the job is done. Instead of answering once, it keeps working — like an intern who checks their own work instead of asking you after every step.

diagram.caption: Perceive → decide → act, on repeat until the job is done.

nodes.blurb: Your request — e.g. “book me a flight under $400”.
nodes.label: Goal

nodes.blurb: Break the goal into steps: search flights, check the calendar, compare prices.
nodes.label: Plan

nodes.blurb: Use tools: search flights, read the calendar, check prices.
nodes.label: Act with tools

nodes.blurb: Finished? No → loop back to planning. Yes → report.
nodes.label: Done?

nodes.blurb: Tell you what happened and what it did.
nodes.label: Report

diagram.title: The agentic loop

edges.label: can trigger
edges.note: Each lap around the loop spends tokens. A stuck loop burns them fast.

example.body: You say “find me a flight under $400 for Friday.” The AI searches flights (act), reads the results (observe), notices the cheap one has a six-hour layover (decide), searches again with a layover filter, and finally books — looping four or five times before reporting back. You asked once; it worked five times.
example.title: Booking a trip while you sleep

footnotes.body: The classic formulation is the ReAct pattern (reason + act). Production loops add planners, verifiers, budgets (max iterations, max tokens), and human-in-the-loop checkpoints before irreversible actions.
footnotes.label: For the technical reader

name: Agentic Loop
tagline: The perceive–decide–act cycle that lets an AI keep working on a task without you.
whyItMatters: This loop is what turns a chatbot into something that can book, file, fix, and follow up. It's also where costs and mistakes compound: every lap around the loop spends tokens and gives the AI another chance to go sideways.
